cmd.help_text:
gil — open one step of thinking, do it for real, write it down and close it.

Every day
  gil start   start the project and open the first Interview
  gil open    open the next step — **saying what you intend to do** (stdin)
  gil close   after the actual work, write the Report and close that step (stdin)

An action step opens with an action contract. GIL never invents its content.

  gil open <<'EOF'
  objective:   what you want to achieve
  next_action: the first thing to do in the real world now (not a gil command)
  done_when:   what you must see to call it done
  EOF

A Cycle is a container, so it opens without a contract — `gil open <kind>`.

One round
  start → open → actual work → close → open → …
  gil judges the boundary between Step and Cycle. You need not memorize which layer you are in.

To see the contract of the current position — **read only, nothing changes.**
  gil open --help    what can open now and the shape of the action contract
  gil close --help   the fields needed to close the current position and what their values mean

When taking over
  gil context   restore the current position in a new session, a handoff or after losing context
  gil status    say where we are in three lines
  gil story     read what has been walked in plain words
  gil monitor   read the current state and its grounds on one screen
  gil monitor --html   the same as one HTML document you can save and open
  gil monitor --serve   keep watching in a browser (Ctrl-C ends it)

When Artifacts were changed and you want them back — **takes no arguments.**
  gil restore   return the working folder to the world the current position requires

How a Report is written — the characters you write are the value. No comments, no quoting, no type conversion.

  gil close <<'EOF'
  problem: to the end of the line as is — #7 and 3.10 are just characters
  next_direction:
    action: close_cycle          (indentation joins names with a dot)
  interpretation: |
    several lines open like this.
  EOF

When closing a Cycle, the field that points at the verdict is an **address** — not the screen's `#4` but:

  outcome_ref: step:C1/S4

`gil open` and `gil close` tell you what to write, right there.

Old names (compatibility)
  gil cycle open · gil cycle close   `gil open` · `gil close` now judge both layers
  gil revisit                        step the revisit already written in a closed verdict
  gil --version                      print the version

Install (Windows)
  gil install    register this executable with Claude Desktop and Codex
  gil doctor     report the registration state, one line per Host (OK · NOT_INSTALLED · MISSING · STALE · ERROR)
  gil uninstall  remove only the gil entry from both settings files
  gil serve      same as `gil mcp --serve`

ctx.explore.after_success: The Experiment closed with success. That success does not complete an approved requirement (requirements of approved revision {revision}: {ids}). Following what was observed, open the next small question linked to the same or another approved requirement with gil_open(kind: experiment) ({skeleton}), or, once the answer, evidence and limits per requirement can be put together, open a Closing Interview with gil_open(kind: interview). Execution contract: exploration (requirement–experiment links) · approved revision {revision} · digest {digest}
Approved requirements and the experiments linked to them (as recorded):
ctx.explore.no_active: Execution contract: exploration (requirement–experiment links). There is no executable approved requirement yet. Get the requirements, scope, constraints and judgment criteria approved in an Interview.
ctx.explore.originals: Original evidence: read a linked experiment's original text with gil_report_read — owner {kind: cycle, ref} returns its Step references and Cycle Report, {kind: step, ref} returns the one Define, Verify, Analysis or Outcome you need. gil_evidence_read reads an evidence file a Verify declared from that Verify's Snapshot; a file of the same name in the working folder may have changed since. Ground the next experiment, and the answer, evidence and limits per requirement reviewed in the Closing Interview, in these original records; do not keep a separate running ‘current answer’ or provisional summary per requirement and use it as a premise for later experiments. A record existing is not a finding that it is true or still valid.
ctx.explore.unresolved: Every requirement is unresolved. An experiment's success only means its own Define held, not that the requirement is complete; whether a failure is a grounded ‘no’ or a judgment that was not reached is told apart in each Cycle Report. The answer, evidence and limits per requirement are judged in a Closing Interview the user approves. The Core does not verify the meaning of the link statements (relevance, readiness, uncertainty).

ctx.file_scope:
[Project file work scope]
Create, modify, delete, move or import Artifact files inside the project only in an Experiment Verify that is actually open. This includes producing and rendering DOCX, PNG and PDF files. At every other position — a Closing Interview, waiting for approval, a boundary with no open Step, a closed Chain — do not change files. Work outside the project, web research that leaves no project file, and reading existing evidence are allowed without this limit. GIL records, approvals and permitted recovery follow the existing tools and contracts; never edit .gil directly. This is Agent guidance, not an OS write block.

ctx.next.blocked: {why}. Read the recorded direction in gil_story. Tell the user why it is blocked.
ctx.next.can_revisit_dev: {cycle} closed as failure · revisit. Call gil_revisit (no arguments) once, then open a new Cycle with gil_open. Revisiting restores Artifacts, so tell the user first.

ctx.next.chain_closed: The Chain is closed. Call gil_open(kind: chain) explicitly only when there is a new topic. Do not call gil_start.
ctx.next.chain_report: Submit the Chain Report with gil_close (verdict · closing_synthesis_ref · handoff_summary). Do not open a new Cycle.
ctx.next.chain_report_approved: Submit the Chain Report with gil_close: verdict: {verdict} — the chain_verdict the user approved in {target}, not the Closing Interview's own success — · closing_synthesis_ref: {target} · handoff_summary. Open no new Cycle or Chain; after it closes, tell the user the verdict, the deliverables and the remaining questions, then stop.
ctx.next.closing_outcome: Open Interview Outcome of the Closing Interview: gil_close (verdict: success · lesson · synthesis_ref · next_direction). The success here means the closing proposal was approved; the approved Chain verdict ({verdict}) is written in the Chain Report, not here. After closing it, close the Interview Cycle Report with next_direction.action: close_chain.
ctx.next.closing_synthesis_closed: The approved closing Synthesis is closed (chain_verdict: {verdict}). Open the Interview Outcome with gil_open(kind: outcome). Its verdict is success because the closing proposal was approved; that is not the Chain verdict. Do not ask for approval or propose again, and open no Experiment.
ctx.next.cycle_close_closing: The Closing Interview's Outcome is closed and its Cycle is still open. Submit the Cycle Report with gil_close (verdict: success · outcome_ref · handoff_summary · next_direction.action: close_chain). That success is this Interview's own verdict, not the Chain's. The Chain Report follows with the approved chain_verdict ({verdict}) as its verdict. Open no Experiment.
ctx.next.cycle_close_experiment: The Outcome is closed and the Experiment Cycle is still open. Submit the Cycle Report with gil_close. Open the next problem after that.
ctx.next.cycle_close_interview: The Outcome is closed and the Interview Cycle is still open. Submit the Cycle Report with gil_close (verdict · outcome_ref · handoff_summary · next_direction). Then follow its receipt; a Closing Interview leads to the Chain Report.
ctx.next.define: Open Define: write only the one question to check and its judgment criterion, then gil_close. Project files change in Verify.
ctx.next.experiment_closed: The Experiment Cycle is closed. If an independent question remains, gil_open(kind: experiment); if the goal must be agreed again, gil_open(kind: interview).
ctx.next.experiment_outcome: Open Experiment Outcome: write verdict, lesson and next_direction, then gil_close. After closing it, close the Cycle Report separately.
ctx.next.generic_open: Open {kind}: when the completion condition is met, gil_close with the observed result.
ctx.next.hypothesis: Open Hypothesis: write the expectation, its basis and the guardrail, then gil_close. After it closes, the next call is gil_open for Verify; do not change project files before that succeeds.
ctx.next.hypothesis_closed: The Hypothesis is closed. Open gil_open(kind: verify) with an action contract. Do not change project files before the open succeeds.
ctx.next.interpretation: Open Interpretation: separate what the answer settled from what remains unknown and gil_close. Do not change project files.
ctx.next.interview_closed: The Interview Cycle is closed too. Open the Experiment for the first agreed question with gil_open(kind: experiment). Do not call gil_start again.
ctx.next.interview_outcome: Open Interview Outcome: judge the approved scope and gil_close (verdict · lesson · synthesis_ref · next_direction). Do not leave it open until the project ends. After closing it, close the Interview Cycle Report separately.
ctx.next.new_chain_interview: Opening Interview of a new Chain: read the previous Chain's verdict and handoff summary in gil_context (and its original Reports when a decision needs them), then open the first question with gil_open(kind: question) and its action contract (objective · next_action · done_when). Start from what was answered, what stayed open and the candidates it left, and agree on the new scope with the user. A candidate in the handoff is not approval: the previous Chain's approval and plan are not reused, and this Chain needs its own. Do not repeat gil_start or Monitor preparation.
ctx.next.new_experiment: New Experiment: open gil_open(kind: define) with an action contract. Handle only one question to check.
ctx.next.new_interview: New Interview: open the first question with gil_open(kind: question) and an action contract (objective · next_action · done_when). Do not repeat gil_start or the Monitor preparation.
ctx.next.nothing: Nothing can be opened or closed here. Read gil_status once.
ctx.next.open_many: Open one of the following with gil_open: {names}. Include an action contract (objective · next_action · done_when).
ctx.next.open_only: Open gil_open(kind: {kind}) with an action contract.
ctx.next.question: Open Question: if the actual user reply has arrived, gil_close with its original text. Otherwise ask the user, end the turn and wait for the answer. Do not change project files.
ctx.next.revisited_dev: Revisited from {from}. Open a new Cycle below this position with gil_open(kind: interview|experiment). Do not repeat gil_revisit.
ctx.next.revisited_product: Revisited from {from}. After confirming in the Monitor that the file restore completed, open a new Cycle with gil_open(kind: interview|experiment). Do not repeat gil_revisit. Resume with gil_revisit only if a saved approved restore was interrupted.

ctx.next.synthesis_closed_outcome: Only the approved Synthesis is closed. Open the Interview Outcome with gil_open(kind: outcome). Do not reopen the Synthesis or ask for approval again.
ctx.next.verify: Open Verify: actually perform the contract's next_action, save the observed results as project files, then gil_close including evidence_files. Chat alone does not close it.
ctx.next.verify_closed: The Verify is closed. Open the place to interpret the saved evidence with gil_open(kind: analysis).

GIL context — what you need to know to continue walking from the current position.

Distance sets the resolution: past Cycles down to the projection that represents each, the current Cycle
down to Step Reports, the current position down to its rules. The Step Graphs of past Cycles are only
folded here; they are not gone and remain preserved in the original Graph.

ctx.report_principles:
[Principles for writing a Report]  (GIL Specification v0.1 “Report writing invariants”)
Write so that a collaborator who took no part in this Node can point to the same subject and grounds alone.
Do not state a subject or conclusion with only undefined abbreviations, internal step codes or issue numbers.
Do not mix observation (verify) with interpretation (analysis); write success and failure claims so they
can be traced to the pre-set criteria and to Report/Artifact evidence.

guide.closed.blocked: Next action: nothing can be done here. Read gil_status once and tell the user why it is blocked.
guide.closed.chain: Next action: the Chain is closed ({verdict}). The Chain Report and handoff summary are preserved. Open no further Cycle or Step in this Chain; tell the user the verdict, the deliverables and the remaining questions. Only when there is a new topic, call gil_open(kind: chain) once, explicitly: that Chain is approved in its own Opening Interview and reuses no earlier approval or plan. Do not call gil_start.
guide.closed.chain_report: Next action: submit the Chain Report with gil_close. Do not open a new Cycle.
guide.closed.close_cycle: Next action: submit this Cycle's Report with gil_close. Do not use gil_cycle(action=close).
guide.closed.closing_outcome_cycle: Next action: submit the Closing Interview's Cycle Report with gil_close (verdict: success · outcome_ref · handoff_summary · next_direction.action: close_chain). That success is the Interview's own verdict because the closing proposal was approved; the approved chain_verdict goes into the Chain Report that follows. Open no Experiment.
guide.closed.experiment_open_cycle: Next action: the Experiment Cycle is closed. If an independent question remains, gil_open(kind: experiment); if the goal must be agreed again, gil_open(kind: interview). Even when all work is done, do not end with a chat report alone: if there is a Chain, open the Closing Interview with gil_open(kind: interview), get the final verdict approved and close the Chain Report.
guide.closed.experiment_open_cycle_explo: Next action: the Experiment Cycle closed with success. That success does not complete an approved requirement. Following what was observed, open the next small question linked to the same or another approved requirement with gil_open(kind: experiment, contract: the requirement link), or, once the answer, evidence and limits per requirement can be put together, open a Closing Interview with gil_open(kind: interview) and have the final verdict approved. Do not end with a chat report alone. Do not re-propose the plan merely to split, re-order or change the method of experiments; agree in an Interview only when the requirement itself changes.
guide.closed.experiment_revisit_dev: Next action: this Cycle closed as failure · revisit. An Artifact restore follows, so tell the user, call gil_revisit (no arguments) once, and then open a new Cycle with gil_open.
guide.closed.experiment_revisit_product: Next action: this Cycle closed as failure · revisit. Open the Monitor, guide the user to review the change list and the preserved location, then wait for the ‘Preserve and revisit’ button. Do not transcribe chat consent as approval or repeat gil_revisit. After the restore completes, open a new Cycle with gil_open. The failure record, evidence and lessons remain.
guide.closed.generic: GIL progress: this close succeeded. Before further work, follow the next action in the receipt below. If a Hypothesis was closed, the next action is gil_open for Verify. Do not change project files before the open is confirmed. If this was a typed close without next guidance, read gil_status once. Do not perform an unrecorded next step first.
guide.closed.hypothesis: Next action: open the Verify with gil_open(kind: verify) and an action contract. Do not change project files before the open succeeds.
guide.closed.interview_open_cycle: Next action: the Interview Cycle is closed too. Open the Experiment for the first agreed question with gil_open(kind: experiment). In the approved-plan profile the first unexecuted item is bound automatically. Do not call gil_start again.
guide.closed.interview_open_cycle_explor: Next action: the Interview Cycle is closed too. This Chain is under the exploration contract, so no item is bound automatically. Read active_plan's revision, digest and requirement ids with gil_plan_read, then open the Experiment for the smallest question that can be judged now with gil_open(kind: experiment, contract: plan_revision · plan_digest · requirement_id · relevance · readiness · uncertainty). Do not call gil_start again.
guide.closed.interview_outcome_cycle: Next action: submit the Interview Cycle Report with gil_close (verdict · outcome_ref · handoff_summary · next_direction). Open the Experiment after that succeeds, and change project files in Verify.
guide.closed.open_kind: Next action: open gil_open(kind: {k}) with an action contract. Do not change project files before a Verify is actually open.
guide.closed.open_many: Next action: open one of the following with gil_open: {kinds}. The receipt below says how to choose.
guide.closed.outcome_cycle: Next action: submit this Cycle's Report with gil_close. If the Verify attached visuals, the Cycle Report also cites them with expected_owner {kind: cycle} and visuals.uses (stored source). Open the next problem after that.
guide.closed.synthesis_outcome: Next action: open the Interview Outcome with gil_open(kind: outcome). Do not ask for approval again or reopen the Synthesis. After closing the Outcome, close the Interview Cycle Report separately as well.
guide.closed.synthesis_question: Next action: not approved. Ask what must change with gil_open(kind: question). The approval of an earlier proposal is not reused.
guide.closed.verify: Next action: open the place to interpret the saved evidence with gil_open(kind: analysis). Do not change project files. If this Verify attached visuals, cite them (owner · asset_id · sha256) as a stored source when closing the Analysis and the Cycle Report.
guide.closing_proposal: If this proposal closes the Chain: the statement gives, for each approved question, the answer reached, its evidence references, the counter-evidence and the limits, read from the linked Experiments' original Reports rather than from memory. Separate what is still unanswered, why this exploration stops now, and candidate follow-up experiments or alternative material. chain_verdict is the verdict the user is asked to approve; open questions are stated, never turned into success, and closing opens no next Chain.
guide.closing_results_first: Show the result first: the Closing Interview's first message presents what was made and what it is for, the actual deliverable with a way to open it (file link, key numbers, real screen or saved capture, changed code and its test result), the verification result and remaining limits, and only then asks whether to close. A file list or “done” is not the result; present partial or missing results truthfully; read the recorded evidence and create no new files there.
guide.context: GIL resume: when continuing this project, follow the one line under {heading} in the context below first. Do not demand GIL steps to answer an unrelated topic. Do not repeat an already closed step and do not call gil_start again on an existing project. Change project files only in an open Verify.
guide.define_exploration: Define under the exploration contract: write not the whole approved requirement this Experiment is linked to, but the one smallest problem that contributes to it and can be carried out and judged now. Phrase a single proposition answerable yes or no as a question, and fix its target, scope and judgment criterion before observing. Activities such as looking into, checking or writing a report are not a problem definition, and having finished an activity does not satisfy the proposition. Do not record an answer that could not be reached for lack of evidence as a grounded no. If the fixed Define is not met, close with failure, revisit, and then open a different small question. A change to the requirement, scope or permission itself is agreed in an Interview, not written as a Define. This experiment's success does not complete the requirement.
guide.define_smallest: Define the smallest problem that can be performed and judged now: the same problem and completion scope as the agreed item for this Experiment (approved-plan profile: the bound current_item), not the Chain goal. Name the inputs at hand, the first action, the observable result and where to stop. Do not bundle independent goals into one Experiment, and do not split a mere preparation with no checkable result of its own into a separate one. Executing part of a large approved item does not complete it, and splitting or replacing an approved item is not supported by the current runtime: say so plainly and change no approved scope. Use one yes/no proposition as a question, not an activity such as inspect or check. Fix its scope and criterion before observing results; an inspection report is not proposition fulfillment, and insufficient evidence is not a supported no. The item-binding rule here is the current runtime constraint; the new stable-requirement/multiple-experiment design is not yet enabled.
guide.dirty_close.dev: If the refusal is dirty: tell the user the change list from the refusal, and if the user chooses to roll back, send the same gil_close after gil_restore. Deliverables made outside a Verify are recreated in the next Experiment's Verify.
guide.dirty_close.product: If the refusal is dirty: this build refuses Artifact rollback (restore). Read the change list in the refusal; move new files to a new preserved location outside the project (to keep their content, close the current position, then recreate them in the next Experiment's Verify and list them in evidence_files), preserve the current content of changed existing files separately and restore them to the baseline content, then send the same gil_close.
guide.explore.after_failure: Exploration contract: the revisit is not skipped even when no file changed. Check that the Outcome's lesson and the Cycle Report tell the location of the cause apart from the restore point, and after the restore open a different small Define linked to the same approved requirement.
guide.file_boundary.applicability: This is Agent guidance for the selected GIL project, not an OS write block. GIL installs no hooks and this does not apply to ordinary shells or other projects.
guide.file_boundary.rules: Create, modify, delete, move or import project files only in a Verify that is actually open. This includes producing and rendering DOCX, PNG and PDF files. Work outside the project and web research that leaves no project file are not covered by this limit.
guide.interpretation_sort: Separate what the user's answers confirmed, your own interpretation or recommendation, and what is still unknown. If an open point still matters for the next item or its approval, open another Question before the Synthesis.
guide.interrupt_honest: When the work cannot be finished: a lost connection or a pending human response is a wait, not an end — leave the open Step as it is and continue later. If the contracted work cannot continue, save an interruption observation that separates what was done, what blocked it and what remains unverified, close Verify with it as evidence, and carry the unverified scope and its reason into Analysis, Outcome and the closing handoff_summary. If the success condition was not evaluated, record that fact as distinct from a refutation. Never dress an interruption up as success or invent evidence; partial result files stay preserved in the Verify Snapshot.
guide.interrupt_honest.end_history: When the work cannot be finished: a lost connection or a pending human response is a wait, not an end — leave the open Step as it is and continue later. If the contracted action cannot be carried out, write what was done, what blocked it and what remains unverified, kept apart, in the Report body (a Verify saves that observation as a file and names it in evidence_files) and close. When the connected close tool offers the unachieved_will input and the project's format records end results (8/9), name the active Will (will:W…) in unachieved_will to end that Will as unachieved; in any other project do not use that input. An unachieved close waives no close condition and skips neither Analysis nor Outcome, and that Experiment then closes only as a failure (Outcome verdict failure · next_direction.action close_cycle). If the success condition was not evaluated, record that fact as distinct from a refutation. Never dress an interruption up as success or invent evidence; partial result files stay preserved in the Verify Snapshot.
guide.interrupt_partial_results: Before revisiting, show the user this Cycle's Verify evidence_files and partial results first. The restore removes those files from the working folder, but they remain in the Snapshot and the preserved location. A transition that keeps the partial results in place and continues is not in the contract yet: do not substitute a fake success or edit records; if needed, report it as a pending user decision.
guide.interview_deepen: Deep interview: ask about the real situation, the inputs, an example and a counter-example of the result, what is in and out of scope, constraints, priority and a completion condition the user can judge. Reuse answers already given and ask first the one open point that changes the next decision; add no question to a request that is already concrete.
guide.opened.analysis: GIL progress: an Analysis is open. Interpret only the saved Verify evidence and gil_close with a non-blank interpretation: do not repeat the Verify observation; write what it means for the hypothesis and what remains uncertain. Do not change project files. If the Verify attached visuals, this close must cite them: send expected_owner and visuals together, and in uses write the Verify receipt's owner, asset_id and sha256 as a stored source (attachments is an empty array, declaration omitted).
guide.opened.chain: GIL progress: the next Chain is open. Its Opening Interview is open with no Step yet. The one next call is gil_context: read the previous Chain's verdict and handoff summary, then gil_open(kind: question) with an action contract to confirm the new topic with the user. Nothing from the previous Chain's approval, plan or re-interview request is reused: in the approved-plan profile, get a new approval with gil_plan_propose in the new Synthesis. Do not call gil_start, and do not change project files in an Interview.
guide.opened.define: GIL progress: a Define is open. Write only the one question to check and its judgment criterion, then gil_close. Project files change in Verify.
guide.opened.experiment: GIL progress: an Experiment Cycle is open. The next call is gil_open(kind: define) with an action contract. Handle one question only, and do not change project files before a Verify is actually open.
guide.opened.generic: GIL progress: do only the 'To do now' below. When the completion condition is met, gil_close with the observed result and move to the next action. Do not keep attaching work with another purpose to this node. An Interview goes only as far as agreeing on the goal. Change project files only in an Experiment Verify that is actually open. Work outside the project and web research that leaves no file are not limited to GIL steps.
guide.opened.hypothesis: GIL progress: a Hypothesis is open. Write the expectation, its basis and the guardrail, then gil_close. After it closes, the next call is gil_open for Verify; do not change project files before that succeeds.
guide.opened.interpretation: GIL progress: an Interpretation is open. Separate what the answer settled from what remains unknown and gil_close. Do not change project files.
guide.opened.interview: GIL progress: an Interview Cycle is open. The next call is gil_open(kind: question) with an action contract. Project files are not changed in an Interview.
guide.opened.interview_outcome: GIL progress: an Interview Outcome is open. Judge the approved scope and gil_close. Do not leave it open until the project ends. After closing it, gil_close the Interview Cycle Report separately.
guide.opened.outcome: GIL progress: an Experiment Outcome is open. gil_close with a verdict, lesson and next_direction grounded in the actual Analysis. After closing it, gil_close the Cycle Report separately.
guide.opened.question: GIL progress: a Question is open. Ask the user and wait for the answer. gil_await_user(project_root, question) is an optional read-only check, not a condition for ending the turn. When the answer arrives, gil_close with its original text. Do not close by writing the user's original request as the response — never close without an actual answer. Do not change project files while waiting. File-free web research, reading existing evidence and unrelated outside work are allowed and do not stand in for the user's answer.
guide.opened.synthesis: GIL progress: a Synthesis is open. Show the proposal statement to the user (in the approved-plan profile, propose first with gil_plan_propose({project_root, draft:{scope, items, synthesis}}) and wait for the Monitor button — scope, items and synthesis go inside draft, and exploration_checklist is a string inside synthesis. A Closing keeps the existing items and adds draft.synthesis.chain_verdict (success or failure)). Wait for the answer. gil_await_user(project_root, question) is an optional read-only check, not a condition for ending the turn. gil_close only with explicit consent. Silence, an earlier request or your own judgment is not approval. Do not change project files while waiting.
guide.opened.synthesis_basis:
{specific}
Proposal input $.draft.synthesis.basis_refs: {location}{rules} In a JSON string a line break is written as \n. Shape example (replace S1/S2 with the real closed references): {example}
guide.opened.synthesis_location: Current Synthesis: {here}, Interview: {cycle}. Check the real closed references with gil_context.
guide.opened.verify: GIL progress: a Verify is open. Now actually perform the contract's next_action. Save the observed results as project files and gil_close including evidence_files. Chat alone does not close it. Leave visual evidence too: plots drawn by code for data, diagrams for structure, real-browser (headless is fine) screenshots for UI/web, comparison tables saved as PNG for file changes, attached through visuals.attachments/uses with declaration attached (AI-generated images are not visual evidence). If no image is truly needed, state concretely in not_needed what replaces it — a one-word reason is refused. In the approved-plan profile, leave both the plan_document file and separate execution evidence. In result write only what was observed (numbers, output, screens, file changes); what it means for the hypothesis belongs to the Analysis interpretation, and success or failure to the Outcome verdict.
guide.plan.approved: Approved plan: revision {revision} was approved. The next call is gil_close (Synthesis) with close_report inserted verbatim. Only after closing in the order gil_open(kind: outcome) → gil_close → gil_close of the Interview Cycle Report do you open gil_open(kind: experiment).
guide.plan.bound: Approved plan: this Experiment is bound to item {item}. In Verify, save document byte-for-byte to a file and name it in plan_document; record the actual work evidence as separate files in evidence_files. Define points at the same problem and completion scope as item {item}; executing only part of it does not complete the item.
guide.plan.changes: Approved plan: changes were requested for revision {revision}. gil_close the Synthesis with close_report (approved: no) and ask what to change in the next Question. A revised proposal is a new revision; the earlier approval is not reused.
guide.plan.cycle_closed: Approved plan: the current Cycle is already closed. The item binding remains as a record. The next call is gil_context. Follow the next action in its reply to continue with a new Cycle or the Chain Report. Do not keep changing project files in a closed Step.
guide.plan.cycle_unknown: Approved plan: the item binding alone cannot confirm that the current Cycle is open. The next call is gil_context. Confirm the actually open Step and the next action, then continue.
guide.plan.linked: Requirement link: this Experiment handles one small question that contributes to approved requirement {item}. The Define is not the whole requirement but a proposition to judge yes or no now. In Verify, save document byte-for-byte to a file and name it in plan_document; record the actual work evidence as separate files in evidence_files. This experiment's success does not complete requirement {item}.
guide.plan.none: Approved plan: neither an open proposal nor an unexecuted item. In an open Synthesis, propose with gil_plan_propose. If every item was executed, open the Closing Interview with gil_open(kind: interview), get the final verdict (chain_verdict) approved and close the Chain Report. Do not end with a chat report alone, and do not invent approval.
guide.plan.pending: Approved plan: no proposal is open. Unexecuted items: {pending}. If the Interview is closed, open the first unexecuted item with gil_open(kind: experiment). If a Synthesis is open, propose with gil_plan_propose first.
guide.plan.reinterview: Approved plan: a re-interview request is preserved. Finish the current Cycle's remaining Steps in receipt order, close the Cycle Report, then get approval again with gil_open(kind: interview). No Experiment can open before then. If a Step is open, closing that Step is the next call.
guide.plan.request_interview: Approved plan: the re-interview request was preserved. Nothing was closed or opened. Continue the currently open Step as the last receipt's next action says; after the remaining Steps and the Cycle Report close in their actual order, get approval again with gil_open(kind: interview). The request is preserved meanwhile, and no new Experiment can open before then. There is no call that cancels the request or aborts the Cycle.
guide.plan.request_saved: Approved plan: the re-interview request was preserved. Nothing was closed or opened.
guide.plan.unsupported: Approved plan: this project is not in the approved-plan profile. Do not demand gil_plan_*. Wait for the user's answer in an ordinary Synthesis. gil_await_user(project_root, question) is an optional read-only check, not a condition for ending the turn.
guide.plan.waiting: Approved plan: proposal revision {revision} was recorded and awaits the Monitor button response. End the turn and wait. gil_await_user(project_root, question) is an optional read-only check, not a condition for ending the turn. Do not substitute chat consent or write approved yourself. Do not change project files or re-propose meanwhile. Check for a response only with gil_plan_read.
guide.propose_brief: Propose short: first the goal, this scope, the key constraints and the decisions to confirm, as statements the user can accept or correct at a glance; then the ordered items, where each question is one performable, checkable problem and each done_when its observable completion, with the inputs, prerequisite, first action and check beside it. An unconfirmed prerequisite becomes the first item. Link statements to the actual Question/Interpretation refs in basis_refs instead of repeating the interview, keep the existing scope/items/synthesis shape, and drop no constraint, risk or uncertainty for brevity.
guide.propose_requirements: Keep an exploration-contract proposal short: first show the goal, this scope, the key constraints and the decisions to confirm as propositions the user can judge right or wrong at a glance. The items are the requirements to approve, not an execution order. Each question is one question this Chain will answer, and each done_when the criteria by which the user will judge that answer. Agree on the data scope, the quality of evidence and how uncertainty and limits will be reported. Do not fix the answer, the pattern to find or the full experiment procedure and order in advance: small experiments are chosen from observation after approval. Instead of repeating the interview, link to the actual Question and Interpretation references with basis_refs, keep the existing scope/items/synthesis shape, and do not drop constraints, risks or uncertainty for the sake of brevity.
guide.refused.close: GIL refusal: nothing was closed. Fix the field named in the reason below using the input skeleton shown there, and send the same gil_close once more; the skeleton is the current contract, so the manual need not be read again for it. If no skeleton is shown or the position is uncertain, read gil_status first. Do not skip other steps or backfill records in bulk.
guide.refused.open: GIL refusal: nothing was opened. Read the reason below and send once more with a kind allowed at the current position and an action contract (objective · next_action · done_when). If the position is uncertain, read gil_status.
guide.refused.plan_close: GIL refusal: nothing was closed. The reason below is the approved plan's state, not a Report input error — do not fix and resend the same gil_close. The one next call is gil_plan_read; follow the next action its reply names (no proposal → gil_plan_propose · waiting → end the turn and wait for the Monitor button · approved → gil_close with close_report verbatim · changes requested → close_report with approved: no, then a Question). Never write approved yourself or treat chat consent as approval.
guide.refused.plan_link: GIL refusal: nothing was opened. The reason below concerns the requirement link. Read active_plan (revision · digest · items) and experiment_link with gil_plan_read, correct the link to one approved requirement and send gil_open(kind: experiment) once more. An unapproved requirement, another Chain's approval or a superseded revision cannot open an Experiment; to change the requirement itself, agree on it in an Interview. Never invent approval.
guide.refused.plan_open: GIL refusal: nothing was opened. The reason below is the approved plan's state, not a kind or contract error — do not change the kind or contract and resend. The one next call is gil_plan_read; follow the next action its reply names (a preserved re-interview request, no approval yet and no pending item each lead somewhere different). Never invent approval.
guide.refused.plan_propose: The proposal was not recorded. Fix the specific cause above. Copy all existing items from gil_plan_read.active_plan.items as they are and add new IDs. Read the connected gil_plan_propose schema for the input shape.
guide.refused.plan_read: GIL refusal: the approval state could not be read. If the reply is uncertain, read gil_plan_read once more. Do not invent an approval or close the Synthesis.
guide.refused.plan_request_interview: GIL refusal: the re-interview request was not recorded. Send it once more from the open Experiment with a reason of 1–4096 bytes. The next call for the current Step is unchanged — continue with the next action of the last receipt.
guide.refused.revisit: GIL refusal: no revisit happened. If the reason is a dirty world, an approved-plan binding or no recorded direction, tell the user that condition. Do not repeat gil_revisit or run restore automatically.
guide.refused.start: GIL refusal: no new project was created. If a project already exists, read gil_context once and continue from the recorded position. Do not repeat gil_start.
guide.report_brief: Write the Report short: what this Step newly established and its key basis; point at saved evidence instead of pasting logs; do not repeat earlier fields or lower-level Reports; keep failure causes, uncertainty and unverified scope.
guide.revisit: GIL revisit complete: the working folder was restored to the target Cycle's world. The next call opens a new Cycle with gil_open(kind: interview|experiment). Do not repeat gil_revisit.
guide.show_monitor: GIL progress: the Monitor display was requested. In a fresh-start flow, call gil_open(kind: question) with the same project_root first and ask. Even without a goal yet, open the Question with an action contract that asks for the goal and the completion criterion. Ask in the new Question and wait for the user's answer (gil_await_user(project_root, question) is an optional read-only check, not a condition for ending the turn) — do not write the user's request down as the answer and move on. On an existing project, continue the currently open step. Whether the screen is actually visible is not confirmed yet.
guide.start: GIL start: this folder is now a GIL project. Before answering in the chat, make the show_gil_monitor call written in the receipt below first, with the scope_id exactly as given. Then open gil_open(kind: question), ask for the goal and wait for the actual answer. gil_await_user(project_root, question) is an optional read-only check, not a condition for ending the turn. Change project files and produce reports only in an open Experiment Verify. File-free web research, reading existing evidence and unrelated outside work are allowed but do not replace GIL completion.
guide.status: GIL position: the one line below starting with 'Next:' is the move available now. Do not call status repeatedly in the same session; make that move.
guide.unachieved_experiment: This Experiment holds a Will that ended as unachieved ({will} · {target}): close the remaining steps without skipping any, and do not turn the unperformed action into a refutation of the question. The Outcome closes only with verdict failure · next_direction.action close_cycle and the Cycle Report only with failure · revisit; a new hypothesis, an in-Experiment revisit and success are refused. To try again, close the Experiment, restore, and try in the next Experiment.

mcp.action_unfinished: The GIL action did not finish. Check the state, then continue.
mcp.await_user: Waiting for user input: {question}. Write this question verbatim at the end of the reply. After the user answers, continue the same step with gil_context. Completion and approval records are unchanged.
mcp.await_user_failed: The user-wait state could not be checked. Confirm the current step with gil_context.
mcp.companion_unavailable: The Monitor connection could not be checked.
mcp.connect_failed: Could not establish the MCP connection: {err}
mcp.inline_default: The Monitor is confirmed only as an inline preview. Do not report fullscreen as done. If the Host does not accept the automatic expansion, guide the user to the widget header's ‘show in another panel’ or the Host's expand button. Display issues and GIL progress are separate; continue with the next GIL call below.
mcp.inline_error: The Monitor is confirmed as an inline preview, but the result of the automatic fullscreen request ended in an error. Do not treat a timeout or connection problem as a specific Host policy. Guide the user to check the connection or ask again with ‘Expand Monitor’. Display issues and GIL progress are separate; continue with the next GIL call below.
mcp.inline_refused: The Monitor is confirmed as an inline preview, and by the App's report the Host answered that it needs a fresh click inside the App. Do not report fullscreen as done. Guide the user to click inside the Monitor card once or press ‘Expand Monitor’. Display issues and GIL progress are separate; continue with the next GIL call below.
mcp.inline_unavailable: The Monitor is confirmed as an inline preview, and this Host surface does not advertise fullscreen. Do not report fullscreen as done. Guide the user to the widget header's ‘show in another panel’ or the Host's expand button. Display issues and GIL progress are separate; continue with the next GIL call below.
mcp.migration_uncertain: The migration result is uncertain. Preserve the records and backups and read only gil_migration_status. Do not retry automatically.
mcp.transition_uncertain: The transition result is uncertain. Do not apply again; read gil_format_transition_check for the actual state. Nothing is retried, reversed or deleted automatically.
mcp.plan_uncertain: The approval record result is uncertain. Check with gil_plan_read.
mcp.prepare_next: Next call: show_gil_monitor({scope}). Preparation alone does not display the screen.
mcp.prepare_unknown: The Monitor preparation result could not be confirmed
mcp.revisit_uncertain: The restore result is uncertain. Re-read from the Monitor. Do not delete the existing preserved copy.
mcp.runtime_failed: Could not set up the MCP runtime: {err}
mcp.should_open: There is no signal that the MCP App Monitor is showing ({state}). Before continuing, call show_gil_monitor({scope}) once. Do not substitute the Companion. Do not say it is displayed merely because the call succeeded.
mcp.show_monitor: GIL Monitor data is prepared. The App starts in horizontal view and, on a Host that advertises fullscreen, requests fullscreen by itself right after connecting and once the Monitor is ready; if it stays inline, it asks again on the user's first click. If nothing changes, the user clicks the Monitor once or presses Expand Monitor. This reply alone does not establish that the screen is displayed or stays displayed.
mcp.start_handoff: Monitor: there is one next call — {call}. The gil open under ‘Run’ above comes after it. The same applies in Codex and in Claude Desktop's Claude Code tab.
mcp.start_monitor_failed: GIL start succeeded but the Monitor preparation failed: {detail}. Do not repeat gil_start. Tell the user about the display failure and continue the recorded Interview. Retry the Monitor only once, with gil_monitor_prepare, and only if the failure was transient.
mcp.start_ok: GIL start succeeded and the Monitor is prepared. There is one next call: {call}. Regardless of Host, it comes before gil_open; copy the arguments as given. Then call gil_open for the first Interview with the same project_root. Do not repeat gil_start or gil_monitor_prepare. Do not assume the screen is visible yet.
mcp.status_unknown: The MCP App Monitor display state could not be checked. Do not report the display as successful. The recorded work result stands.
mcp.unachieved_refused: The unachieved end request was not accepted. Nothing was closed and no record changed. Read the reason below and check the active Will and the last ended Will with gil_status or gil_context. Do not repeat the same request automatically.
mcp.unconfirmed: The MCP App Monitor did not respond to two display requests. Stop reopening automatically and report the display problem. Do not open the Companion automatically.
mcp.visual_uncertain: Whether it was confirmed is unknown. Check with gil_report_visuals and do not repeat the close.
mcp.workspace_uncertain: The workspace preparation result is uncertain. Check whether the folder exists and do not repeat.

plan_tool.next:
{next}
A new Interview proposal copies all of active_plan.items verbatim (executed items included) and adds new IDs. Order and scope may change with a new approval, but an existing item's question/done_when cannot. active_plan is the executable approved revision and is null until one exists. document is the UTF-8 original of the approved revision bound when the Experiment opened. It is null before binding, and neither a read nor a failed close creates it. If the current Experiment has a binding but document is null, do not write a summary instead; check the current connection and state. Save files only in a Verify that is actually open. One Experiment is bound to exactly one current_item. executed_cycles is an open binding; the proof of success is that Cycle Report.
plan_tool.next_exploration:
{next}
This Chain is under the exploration execution contract (contract: exploration). active_plan.items are the approved requirements, not an execution order. An Experiment opens with the six fields of experiment_link in the contract of gil_open(kind: experiment); nothing is bound automatically. requirements shows, as recorded, the experiments linked to each requirement and the verdict of their Cycle Reports. An experiment's success does not complete a requirement, and pending only lists requirements no experiment is linked to yet. Whether a requirement is met is approved by the user in a Closing Interview (requirement_resolution). Do not create a new proposal merely to split, re-order or change the method of experiments. Only when the requirement, scope or permission itself changes, copy all of active_plan.items verbatim in an Interview and get a new approval. document is the UTF-8 text of the approved revision linked when the Experiment opened; save it to a file only in an actually open Verify. The Core does not verify the meaning of relevance, readiness or uncertainty.
